Five repeat confirmation follows independent thread and SLEPc configuration screening; all nine thread selections were the original 16-thread default.
Initial queued thread guard exited 75 on lock wait before starting a numerical job; retried with a longer lock wait.
The large single-repeat comparison is against the untuned 1x16 baseline. Independent reference completeness is unknown for both; residuals and returned sets agree.

The small near-singular SLEPc profile uses a matrix-norm-based internal target perturbation; acceptance still uses the original target, k and tolerance. This absolute-target profile is only for this query.

Band LU is a private SciPy prototype, not integrated in hsolve; invalid random-RHS solves are not evidence of speedup. The initial interrupted microbenchmark and the completed rerun are separate batches.
Only SLEPc Krylov-Schur/MUMPS compared here; this is not a proof against every open-source solver.
